---
title: "Schedule"
---

A schedule of topics and readings is provided below. Each week will cover a single topic or group of topics. You should treat the readings as a reference and as a more detailed exposition of the topics discussed in lecture. Consult the readings when you want to know more or want a slightly different approach to explaining a particular topic.

Monday lectures will typically introduce the core theory for the week's topic while Wednesday lectures will go into greater detail and work through applications. You should make sure to review the readings prior to that week's lectures with an aim towards completing them before Wednesday's lecture.

All hyperlinks to papers are either to the published version of the paper (if published) or to the working paper. You should use your university library access to obtain the full version if the article is not open access. Likewise, textbook readings will be to the free/open version of the book (if available) or to the UW-Madison university library eBook.

## Week 1: Course Introduction and Review

*Wednesday, September 2*

**Topics:**

- What is a statistical model and what is it good for?
- Review of estimands, estimators and their properties
- Review of linear regression

**Readings:**

- **Review:** Chapters 1-7; Gelman, Andrew, Jennifer Hill, and Aki Vehtari. 2020. [*Regression and Other Stories*.](https://avehtari.github.io/ROS-Examples/index.html) Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

## Week 5: Bayesian Inference

*Monday, September 28 & Wednesday, September 30*

**Topics:**

- Principles of posterior inference
- How to write a Bayesian model
- Quantities of interest: posterior mode, posterior mean, credible intervals
- Estimation and inference via Markov Chain Monte Carlo

**Readings:**

- Chapter 9; Gelman, Andrew, Jennifer Hill, and Aki Vehtari. 2020. [*Regression and Other Stories*.](https://avehtari.github.io/ROS-Examples/index.html) Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
- Chapters 10-11; Gelman, Andrew, John Carlin, Hal Stern, David Dunson, Aki Vehtari, and Donald Rubin. 2013. [*Bayesian Data Analysis*.](http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/book/) 3rd ed. Boca Raton: Chapman and Hall/CRC.

**Problem Set 2** assigned Wednesday, September 30 -- due Wednesday, October 14.

## Week 6: Multilevel Regression Models

*Monday, October 5 & Wednesday, October 7*

**Topics:**

- "Hierarchical" regression models -- random slopes/random intercept models
- Estimation via MCMC in [Stan](https://mc-stan.org/)
- Interpreting and analyzing results

**Readings:**

- Park, David K., Andrew Gelman, and Joseph Bafumi. 2004. "Bayesian Multilevel Estimation with Poststratification: State-Level Estimates from National Polls." *Political Analysis* 12 (4): 375-385.
- Chapters 9, 11, and Appendix A; Gelman, Andrew, Jennifer Hill, and Aki Vehtari. 2020. [*Regression and Other Stories*.](https://avehtari.github.io/ROS-Examples/index.html) Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
- Chapter 15; Gelman, Andrew, John Carlin, Hal Stern, David Dunson, Aki Vehtari, and Donald Rubin. 2013. [*Bayesian Data Analysis*.](http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/book/) 3rd ed. Boca Raton: Chapman and Hall/CRC.

- Bürkner, Paul-Christian. 2019. ["Bayesian Item Response Modeling in R with brms and Stan."](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.09501) arXiv:1905.09501.
